newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Familes seek Pakistan sailors' release in Vietnam.
newsitem.headline: Familes seek Pakistan sailors' release in Vietnam.

text.p: Families of six Pakistani sailors stranded in Vietnam for two years on a vessel detained in Ho Chi Minh City urged Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif on Sunday to arrange their release.

The sailors have not been paid for two years and are not allowed to leave the confiscated ship before its auction to settle port dues and wage claims, one family member told reporters in Karachi on Sunday.
The sailors were hired in August 1995 by a Karachi-based shipping agent to serve on the foreign flag vessel M.V. Golden Fortune. The agent was not available for comment.

"Misfortunes struck the seafarers immediately after they joined the ship at Singapore to sail for Vietnam," the appeal said. The ship owner, whose identity "is yet to be established", stopped paying wages to the crew and officers, it said.
Vietnamese authorities arrested the ship but "took their own time to decide what to do next" to recover port dues owed as well as wages of the sailors.

"After several months of unsuccessful efforts to contact the owner, a court in Ho Chi Minh City finally decided to confiscate the vessel. But many more months went by before the court finished the proceedings on wage claims without a firm decision and the concerned authorities initiated formalities to auction the vessel.

"Now for the past saveral months bids are being invited and reinvited to obtain the desired price. The six Pakistanis on the ship and six others from Bangladesh have been told to expect payment of their wages only after the ship has been auctioned, according to a formula the court has yet to decide.

"The crew and officers cannot abandon the ship even if they so wish and can arrange air passage. They have to serve as sentinels in outer anchorage and to hand over the vessel to the new buyer whenever one is found."
